macro.regime: Tentative risk rebound, elevated event risk into a stacked catalyst week
macro.narrative: Levels below are as of Friday 21 Aug's US close (S&P 7,674.37 +0.43%, VIX 15.13 -5.5%) -- the whole weekend passed with zero new equity/bond sessions and Asia has not opened yet this Monday. What changed is positioning ahead of three stacked binary catalysts this week rather than any confirmed new print: Treasury's Iran-sanctions rollout (2pm ET Monday, publicly scheduled since Fri 21 Aug -- Bessent's 'toughest sanctions in history' and China-Gulf-energy framing trace to a Thu 20 Aug CNBC interview, not a Sunday one; his genuinely Sunday-dated contribution was an FT op-ed calling it an 'economic D-Day'), Nvidia's FQ2 earnings (Wed 26 Aug after close, the cleanest single read on AI-capex durability), and new Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (Fri 28 Aug, which he has previewed as 'structural, not near-term guidance'). Oil already re-rated on the sanctions anticipation (Brent/WTI +5-6% on the week) before giving back part of that move at Sunday's Globex reopen; crypto similarly gave back roughly a third of Friday's surge over the weekend (BTC ~$76,000 Sunday vs $78,335 Friday close) on thin weekend liquidity -- levels, not closes. Net: trim risk-on conviction modestly ahead of resolution rather than extending into the rebound.

drivers.factor: Iran sanctions rollout (Mon 24 Aug, 2pm ET) now explicitly threatens China as a secondary target
drivers.read: Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sunday 23 Aug FT op-ed ('economic D-Day,' 'the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary') is genuinely new; the harder line quoted elsewhere this week -- 'toughest sanctions in history' and naming China as the buyer of ~90% of Iran's oil while declining to rule out direct targeting -- traces to Thursday 20 Aug's CNBC interview, not Sunday. Iran's security chief Rezaei threatened to halt Hormuz flow if Gulf states join the sanctions, and Iran's parliament advanced a Hormuz transit-fee law over the weekend -- genuine counter-escalation.

drivers.factor: Jackson Hole (27-29 Aug) is the next binary catalyst -- Warsh's untested debut keynote
drivers.read: New Fed Chair Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote Fri 28 Aug, 10am ET ('Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'); he has told reporters the remarks will focus on 'long-term structural questions, not near-term guidance' -- tempering, not eliminating, hawkish-surprise risk versus a BofA survey pricing a neutral-tone consensus.

drivers.factor: Nvidia FQ2 earnings (Wed 26 Aug after close) is now the week's second binary catalyst
drivers.read: The cleanest single read on whether the AI-capex-fatigue narrative behind the mid-week (19-20 Aug) selloff is real. Nvidia is separately providing up to $105B of financing for an OpenAI Ohio data center -- a sign hyperscaler capex intensity is still accelerating, a mild counterweight to the fatigue narrative heading into the print.

drivers.factor: Credit spreads priced for perfection into a heavy September issuance calendar

The G7/Pentagon/DOE rare-earth policy tailwind (MP +9.1%/UUUU +8.9% Fri) is unchanged and now sits adjacent to Monday's China-adjacent Iran-sanctions headlines.
